body:
From the pre-release security review of the server's network interface
(2026-07-26). Post-1.8.1.

## Problem

_add_security_headers (__init__.py:232) sets X-Content-Type-Options and
Referrer-Policy on every owned response, and CSP + X-Frame-Options on HTML — but
sets no cache directives at all. Confirmed on a live response:

    GET /api/v1/settings  200
      Content-Type: application/json
      X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
      Referrer-Policy: no-referrer
      (no Cache-Control, no Pragma, no Vary)

Under RFC 9111 a 200 response to a GET with no explicit freshness information
may be cached heuristically by a shared cache. A TLS-terminating reverse proxy
is a mandatory part of this deployment (server/README.md:332), so a shared cache
is exactly what sits in front of this server.

Affected authenticated GETs: /settings, /lists, /lists/<id>/members (member
email addresses), /account/sessions, /admin/users (every account's email).

Most pointed, though POSTs are not heuristically cached and so are lower risk:
- POST /login returns the bearer token in the body
- POST /admin/users/<id>/reset-password returns a PLAINTEXT password in the body

## Fix

In _add_security_headers, add `Cache-Control: no-store` (setdefault, matching
the existing convention so an operator-set header still wins) for responses that
are not the cacheable static assets.

Careful: the hook is app-wide and self-limits to owned endpoints. The web client
assets deliberately carry long max-age (webapp.py ASSET_MAX_AGE) and the APK
carries APK_MAX_AGE, and web_index sets no-cache explicitly — none of those must
be clobbered. setdefault already protects them since each sets Cache-Control
itself, but this needs an explicit test rather than trust.

## Verification

Assert no-store on the authenticated JSON endpoints above, AND assert the asset
/ APK / index routes keep their existing caching headers unchanged.
title: headers: no Cache-Control on authenticated JSON (tokens and reset passwords included)
